purpose: Directly compare the Magnicon XXF-1 Connector Box 10 kHz anti-alias LPF OFF hypothesis against the documented LPF ON hypothesis under the same relaxed thermal-backbone profile, with c2 fixed to zero in both branches.

magnicon_filter.manual_statement: Connector-box anti-alias filters are second-order Bessel, cutoff 10 kHz +/-2.5%.
magnicon_filter.off_semantics: Diagnostic LPF-OFF branch: the Magnicon connector-box 10 kHz stage is unity for both main and alias paths. The profiled cutoff coordinate is intentionally retained but inert so ON and OFF have exactly the same nuisance-parameter count.
magnicon_filter.on_semantics: Documented LPF-ON branch: second-order phase-normalized Bessel with a shared cutoff profiled only over 10 kHz +/-2.5%.

guardrail: This is an acquisition-state diagnostic, not evidence that the historical connector-box LPF was actually OFF. A materially better OFF fit would make the measurement-time filter state a high-priority laboratory check. A poor OFF fit would disfavor the simple ON/OFF explanation but would not rule out a bypass noise source, lead-lag response, FLL dynamics, or frequency-dependent bias/readout impedance.
